title: Assertion Functions
summary: Tell TypeScript that a condition must be true after a check succeeds.

subtopics.title: Write an assertion signature
subtopics.explanation: An assertion function declares that if it returns normally, a condition is true. Use `asserts value is User` when a check proves a value has a particular type. TypeScript then narrows the value after the call, just as it would inside a successful `if` branch.

subtopics.title: Make the runtime check truthful
subtopics.explanation: TypeScript trusts the assertion signature; it does not inspect the function body to prove the claim. The implementation must check the value and throw when the condition fails. If it returns without validating, later code can treat invalid data as safe and fail at runtime.

subtopics.title: Narrow unknown input after validation
subtopics.explanation: An assertion function is useful at a boundary where data starts as `unknown`, such as a JSON response. After validation succeeds, TypeScript lets the caller use the narrower type. Keep the assertion next to the real checks so future code changes do not make its promise inaccurate.

subtopics.title: Report failed validation
subtopics.explanation: When a value fails the check, throw an error that explains which condition was not met. Do not return normally, because a normal return tells TypeScript the assertion succeeded. At an API boundary, include safe context for debugging without exposing private input values.

subtopics.title: Avoid unchecked type promises
subtopics.explanation: An assertion function is not a shortcut for silencing a type error. First validate the value at runtime, then assert the type that the validation actually proves. Use a type predicate when callers need a true-or-false result instead of an exception-based check.

foundations.overview: An assertion function checks a value at runtime and uses an asserts return type to inform TypeScript that the checked condition now holds. The function must really throw when the condition fails; the type annotation alone cannot make an unsafe check safe.
foundations.mentalModel: A bouncer checks an ID before allowing someone past the door.
foundations.whyItMatters: It connects a runtime validation step to safer types afterward.

keyTakeaways: The implementation must verify the claimed condition.
Throw a useful error when validation fails.
Do not use assertions to silence a type error without checking.

codeLab.title: Assert a Non-Empty Name
codeLab.instructions: Write an assertion function that checks an unknown value is a non-empty string before returning it.
codeLab.expectedOutput: The type checker accepts safe values and reports mismatches at compile time.
hints: Keep external values typed as unknown until you check them.
Use a type feature that preserves the exact information you need.
